source: NCERT-aligned UPSC Ecology & Environment (Class XI), Ch. 12 (Renewable Energy and Sustainable Development).

sections.heading: 1. Conventional vs Non-Conventional Energy
points: **Conventional (non-renewable):** coal, petroleum, natural gas, nuclear — finite, polluting (except partly nuclear), cause GHG emissions.
**Non-conventional (renewable):** **solar, wind, hydro, biomass/biogas, geothermal, tidal, ocean thermal** — clean, inexhaustible.
Renewables are key to **energy security and reducing carbon emissions**.

sections.heading: 2. Major Renewable Sources
points: **Solar** — India has huge potential; **National Solar Mission**; solar parks (e.g. Bhadla, Rajasthan).
**Wind** — India is among the top wind-power producers (Tamil Nadu, Gujarat).
**Biomass/Biogas** — from organic waste; rural energy.
**Hydropower** — large and small (mini/micro) hydel; **tidal** (Gulf of Kachchh) and **geothermal** (Puga, Ladakh).

sections.heading: 3. India's Initiatives and Targets
points: **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)** promotes renewables.
India's climate commitments (Paris/NDCs) and the target of large **non-fossil energy capacity**; **'Panchamrit'** goals (net-zero by 2070).
**International Solar Alliance (ISA)** — launched by India and France (HQ in Gurugram) to promote solar energy globally.
**One Sun One World One Grid (OSOWOG)** and **National Green Hydrogen Mission**.

sections.heading: 4. Sustainable Development Goals
points: **Sustainable development** balances **economic, social and environmental** needs for present and future generations.
The **17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs, 2015–2030)** — including affordable clean energy (SDG 7), climate action (SDG 13), life on land/below water (SDG 14/15).
**Circular economy, energy efficiency, and green technology** support sustainability.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Renewables: solar, wind, hydro, biomass, geothermal, tidal, ocean thermal.
MNRE = nodal ministry; National Solar Mission (under NAPCC).
International Solar Alliance (ISA) = India + France; HQ Gurugram.
India's net-zero target = 2070 ('Panchamrit').
SDGs = 17 goals (2015–2030); SDG 7 = affordable clean energy.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Nuclear energy is non-renewable** (conventional), though low-carbon.
The **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** was co-founded by **India and France** (HQ in Gurugram, India).
India's **net-zero target is 2070**.
There are **17 Sustainable Development Goals** (2015–2030).
